canonical.title: All Nodes at Distance K
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/3. Hard/05. All nodes at distance K.cpp

narrative.title: The Radio Check Distress Sweep
narrative.scenario: A mountain rescue network is laid out as a binary tree of relay posts. When a post sends a distress ping, dispatch must name every relay exactly k hops away — counting along child links and the parent link alike — so neighbouring teams can be paged at once. Hops shorter or longer than k stay silent, and the call order doesn't matter.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child), an integer target — the value of the origin post — and an integer k, the exact hop distance.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the values of all nodes at exactly distance k from the target, in any order.

testCases.explanation: Two hops from 5 reach its parent 3's other child 1, and 5's grandchildren 7 and 4.
Three hops from 5 lands on the root 3's two children 0 and 8.

hintLevels: Level 1: A tree only lets you walk downward — to wander back up you first need a way to find each node's parent.
Level 2: One pass records every parent; a second BFS from the target then spreads across all three directions, skipping burned nodes.
Level 3: Stop expanding once the wave has travelled k rings; whatever sits in the queue is exactly the answer set.
